refused.reader-disagreement-metric: content_f1 reaches 0.000 between clean readers (single-word and digit-only cases): any threshold above zero misses, and a threshold at zero fires on clean files — no value separates, so the metric form is not shipped; the page-empty form is deterministic and ships

rule: value = max(declared floor, clean-set maximum); a separation of at least 0.20 between the clean set and the planted set is required, and a signal that does not separate is refused and not shipped

lam_alef_min_runs.source: declared policy: a transposition density is judged only on a reading with at least 200 Arabic runs; both measured populations are inside it (calibration 473-488 runs, clean 1121-1141), and below it one quoted example is 1/n, not a rate

lam_alef_rate_per_1000.source: derived: geometric midpoint of the two measured bounds (sqrt(clean_max x broken_min)). Clean maximum 0.88 per 1000 runs (doc:report, quoting the defect once in 1140 runs); calibration minimum 43.03 per 1000 (poppler; pdfium 43.66, mupdf 43.12). sqrt(0.8795*43.03)=6.15 -> 6.2. Artifact: docs/checker-v0/measurements/lam-alef-separation.json; scripts/test_lam_alef_separation.py re-derives the value from that artifact

lexical_min_runs.source: declared policy: a reading with fewer than 20 Arabic runs is not judged for lexical validity (it can be neither passed nor failed)

lexical_validity.source: derived: clean_set_minimum - 0.20 (higher = better); clean minimum 0.8684 (governing doc:report); 4 document(s) of 8 judged clean files (the other 62 are below the 20-run floor; all judged minimum 0.8333). The planted letter-swap is the negative side. The calibration lesson's defect is a measured lam-alef transposition, not lexical-only (measurements/lam-alef-separation.json); its lexical ratio is above this floor and is NOT repaired by lowering the threshold.

min_arabic_chars.source: arafix DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS["min_arabic_chars"] (MIT). Used twice, declared: (a) arafix does not judge orientation on a text with fewer Arabic characters, (b) the report asks «is this an Arabic document?» below it (a low finding, not a high one)

segment_order_min.source: derived: clean maximum + 1 (declared floor 2). The clean set (70 files) measures at most 1 reversed segment(s) per reader, 7 in 7 file(s) across all readers — reader findings on clean files (a reader that reverses a segment around a number or a Latin run), not file defects. Broken side, measured: the ZATCA SDK's 16 PDF/A-3 samples give pdfium 2-7 per affected file (measurements/segment-order.json), and the signal fires at count >= value, so 1 < 2 separates. A reader signal: it never raises the file

tounicode_gap_ratio.source: declared policy: one unmapped drawn code in a hundred is a high risk; the clean set measures 0, so value = max(0.01, clean maximum)
